Online Reputation Monitoring: Tools, Alert Thresholds and a Weekly Routine

By RMA — Web Reputation Agency

Online reputation monitoring is a routine, not a piece of software: you define what to watch, connect a few free and paid tools to those sources, set thresholds that trigger action and review everything on a fixed weekly schedule. For most Italian companies a mix of Google Alerts, Search Console, review platform notifications and one social listening tool covers the essentials, provided someone owns the process.

What to monitor: the five source groups

Effective monitoring covers the places where people form an opinion about you, not every mention on the internet. In practice these fall into five groups, and each needs its own method because the tools that catch a news article will not catch a TikTok video.

  • Search results for the brand, product names and key people, including autocomplete suggestions and "People also ask" boxes on Google.it.
  • Review platforms: Google Business Profile, Trustpilot, TripAdvisor, Booking, Amazon or sector marketplaces.
  • News and blogs, both national outlets and local papers in the cities where you operate.
  • Social networks and forums, including Facebook groups, Reddit, LinkedIn and video platforms.
  • AI answers from ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews when asked about your company.

For each group, list the exact queries and accounts to watch: the brand name with and without the legal form (S.r.l., S.p.A.), common misspellings, the founder's name, product names and words Italian users add when they complain, such as "truffa", "opinioni" or "rimborso".

Free reputation monitoring tools that cover the basics

A small business can run solid brand mention monitoring without spending anything on software. The free layer is limited in coverage, but it is reliable and easy to maintain.

Google Alerts and manual searches

Google Alerts sends an email when new indexed pages contain your query. Use quotation marks for exact names, set the region to Italy and the language to Italian, and create separate alerts for each person and product. Alerts miss a lot, so complement them with a monthly manual check of page one in a private browser window.

Google Search Console

Search Console shows which queries bring visitors to your own site. A sudden rise in impressions for "brand + truffa" or "brand + problemi" is an early signal that people are searching for negative information, often before the content itself reaches page one.

Platform notifications

Google Business Profile, Trustpilot and most booking platforms notify owners of new reviews by email or app. Make sure these go to a shared mailbox rather than to one employee who might leave or go on holiday.

Paid tools and when they are worth it

Paid reputation monitoring tools become worthwhile when the volume of mentions exceeds what a person can read, or when social media and video carry most of the conversation. Their value lies in aggregation, sentiment scoring and historical data.

Tool typeWhat it addsWho needs it
Review management dashboardAll ratings in one place, reply workflow, location comparisonChains, franchises, multi-site clinics
Social listening platformPublic posts, comments and some forums with sentimentConsumer brands, public figures
Media monitoring servicePrint, online and broadcast press including paywalled outletsListed and regulated companies
Rank tracker for branded queriesDaily positions of every page-one resultAnyone with an active negative result

No tool covers private groups, messaging apps or closed communities. Sentiment scores in Italian are also less accurate than in English, especially with irony and regional expressions, so automatic labels must always be checked by a person before anyone acts on them.

Setting alert thresholds that trigger action

Thresholds turn monitoring into decisions: they define which signals need an immediate reaction, which go into the weekly review and which are simply recorded. Without them, teams either react to everything or ignore warnings until it is too late.

A practical three-level model works for most Italian companies. Level one, immediate escalation, covers any mention involving safety, legal accusations, data breaches, a news article on page one or a post spreading quickly. Level two, response within 24 to 48 hours, covers a cluster of negative reviews within a few days, a drop in average rating, or a new negative autocomplete suggestion. Level three, recorded for the weekly review, includes isolated complaints and neutral press. Patterns such as several new one-star reviews from accounts with no history are typical warning signs, which we describe in our article on signs that a reputational attack is being prepared.

A threshold is only useful if a named person receives the alert and knows what to do next. Ownership matters more than the choice of tool.

A weekly online reputation monitoring routine

Thirty to sixty minutes a week is enough for most businesses if the routine is fixed. A Monday morning slot works well, because weekend reviews and posts are already visible.

  1. Read all new alerts and review notifications from the past seven days.
  2. Reply to reviews that are still unanswered, following the agreed tone.
  3. Check page one for the main branded queries and note any new or moved result.
  4. Look at Search Console for unusual queries containing the brand.
  5. Ask two or three AI assistants a standard question about the company and save the answers.
  6. Update a simple log with date, source, sentiment, level and action taken.

Once a month, the log is summarised for management: rating trend per platform, new results on page one, recurring complaint themes and open issues. Recurring themes are often operational, such as delivery delays or billing, and belong to the department that can fix them rather than to marketing. The AI check deserves particular attention, since generative answers increasingly shape first impressions, as explained in our analysis of AI Overviews and reputation management.

Keeping records that hold up later

Monitoring data becomes evidence when content turns out to be defamatory or part of a coordinated attack. Screenshots should show the full URL, date and time; for serious cases in Italy, a certified copy by a notary or a forensic acquisition gives the material legal value in proceedings under art. 595 c.p. or in a removal request to a platform.

Keep the log for at least the duration of any possible legal action, and store personal data of reviewers only as long as needed, in line with GDPR principles. Good records also make it easier to brief external partners, which is part of the preparation we recommend in our guide on protecting reputation before problems arise.
